column1: # boru Language Specification: Recursion (fn frames, teardown, tail shapes)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Pins the observable semantics of fn-call frames that tail-call
# optimisation must preserve bit-for-bit (design/legacy/TCO-STAGED.10.ignore
# Stage 0): param/local/capture teardown, per-frame args visibility,
# ReturnCheck behaviour, frames that accrete values, forwards pending
# below a call, and flow control crossing fn frames. Depths stay well
# below the engine's resource guards — the resource shape itself
# (tape growth per call, the exhaustion ceiling) is pinned in
# lang/go/recursion_pin_test.go, not here.
# §1  self-recursion, NON-tail — the add forward pends below each call,
#     so these frames must always nest (never a TCO candidate)
def s fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [0] [n add (s (n sub 1))]]] s 10
column3: non-tail self-recursion (pending add below the call)

column1: def s fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [0] [n add (s (n sub 1))]]] s 500
column3: deeper non-tail recursion, well under the guards

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] 5 add (inc 1)
column3: minimal pending-forward-below shape: add must consume the frame result

column1: def g fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] def x (g 41) x
column3: def parked below a call consumes the frame result and binds AFTER frame teardown

column1: # §2  self-recursion, tail position — the accumulator idiom; covered by
#     the tail-call elimination guarantee (REFERENCE.md "Recursion and
#     tail calls"), so depth is bounded by CPU, not space. Results must
#     be identical with elimination on or off
def s2 fn [[n:Integer acc:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [acc] [s2 (n sub 1) (acc add n)]]] s2 10 0
column3: tail self-recursion (accumulator idiom)

column1: def s2 fn [[n:Integer acc:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [acc] [s2 (n sub 1) (acc add n)]]] s2 500 0
column3: deeper tail self-recursion

column1: def s2 fn [[n:Integer acc:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [acc] [s2 (n sub 1) (acc add n)]]] s2 5000 0
column3: guarantee witness: depth past any per-frame budget (the resource proofs at depth 10000+ under tiny tape ceilings live in the Go pins)

column1: # §3  mutual recursion — tail calls whose callee differs from the caller
def isod fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [false] [isev (n sub 1)]]] def isev fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [true] [isod (n sub 1)]]] isev 10
column3: mutual tail recursion, even probe

column1: def isod fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [false] [isev (n sub 1)]]] def isev fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [true] [isod (n sub 1)]]] isod 10
column3: mutual tail recursion, odd probe

column1: def isod fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [false] [isev (n sub 1)]]] def isev fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [true] [isod (n sub 1)]]] isev 500
column3: deeper mutual recursion

column1: # §4  args — every frame sees its OWN per-call args list
def f fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [args.0 add args.1]] f 3 4
column3: args.N reads the current frame's args in sig order

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [args.0] [f (n sub 1)]]] f 3
column3: the innermost frame's args.0 is ITS arg, not an outer frame's

column1: # §5  frame teardown — params, body-locals, and captures are undone on
#     exit (the cleanup tail TCO would run eagerly)
def g fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def loc 42 n add loc]] g 1
column3: a body-local def is usable within the body

column1: def g fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def loc 42 n add loc]] g 1 loc
column3: …and is torn down when the frame exits

column1: ([n:Integer] => [def lk 9 n add 1]) 5 lk
column3: anonymous-Function dispatch tears down body-locals too

column1: def g2 fn [[pq:Integer] [Integer] [pq]] g2 8 pq
column3: params are undefined after the frame exits

column1: # §6  closures — captures are construction-time snapshots, stable
#     across recursive calls (TCO safety property 2)
def out1 fn [[] [Integer] [def x 7 def go fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [x] [go (n sub 1)]]] go 3]] out1
column3: a captured local stays visible through a chain of recursive calls

column1: def mk2 fn [[x:Integer] [Function] [([x:Integer] => [x add 1])]] 10 (mk2 5) apply
column3: a param shadows a same-named capture (innermost binding wins)

column1: # §7  frames that accrete values — each level leaves a value below the
#     recursive call; such frames are NOT constant-space-able and must
#     keep nesting under any TCO
def m fn [[n:Integer] [] [if (n lte 0) [] [n mul 2 m (n sub 1)]]] m 3
column3: a value parked below the call survives per level, outermost last

column1: def v fn [[x:Integer] [] []] v 1 99
column3: a void callee leaves nothing; execution continues cleanly

column1: # §8  ReturnCheck — declared returns are enforced per frame
def h fn [[n:Integer] [Number] [n]] h 5
column3: a conforming subtype return passes (Integer ⊑ Number)

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [n]] f 1
column3: a non-conforming return is rejected, naming the fn

column1: def r2 fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n n]] r2 1
column3: surplus return values are rejected by count

column1: # §9  flow control crossing fn frames — break/continue raised inside a
#     callee unwind through the frame to the enclosing loop
def b fn [[n:Integer] [] [if (n gt 1) [break] []]] for [1 5] [b i i]
column3: break inside a callee exits the enclosing for

column1: def c fn [[n:Integer] [] [if (n eq 2) [continue] []]] for [1 4] [c i i]
column3: continue inside a callee skips the current iteration

column1: # §10 dynamic reads of an enclosing frame's bindings — outer frames'
#     params and body-locals stay visible to the callee chain until
#     the frame unwinds (innermost binding wins). The recursive-local-
#     fn idiom and loop-carried reads depend on this; any eager frame
#     teardown must decline these shapes (the TCO name-coverage gate)
def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [acc2] [def acc2 n f (n sub 1)]]] f 2
column3: the base branch reads the PREVIOUS frame's body-local (loop-carried dynamic read)

column1: def g fn [[] [Integer] [n]] def f2 fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [g]] f2 42
column3: a callee dynamically reads the caller's param (no capture: g is module-level)

column1: def out2 fn [[] [Integer] [def go2 fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [99] [go2 (n sub 1)]]] go2 3]] out2
column3: a locally-defined fn resolves its own name through the enclosing frame's binding while recursing

column1: # §11 module fn recursion — a module-preamble fn recurses on the MODULE
#     registry's sub-engine tape (one CallBoru boundary crossing per
#     entry); results must be identical whether or not its frames elide
import module [def fac fn [[n:Integer acc:Integer] [Integer] [if (n lte 0) [acc] [fac (n sub 1) (acc mul n)]]] export "MR" {fac: fac/v}] MR.fac 10 1
column3: intra-module tail recursion through an exported preamble fn

column1: import module [def aod fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [false] [aev (n sub 1)]]] def aev fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [true] [aod (n sub 1)]]] export "MR" {aev: aev/v}] MR.aev 9
column3: mutual tail recursion between module-preamble fns

column1: # §12 fn-valued param/capture shadowing — a named param (or capture)
#     whose value is a Function and whose NAME collides with a live
#     CALLER binding must SHADOW that binding (a fresh frame entry the
#     teardown pops to restore the caller's), never replace it. The bug
#     (design/legacy/ACCESSOR-SPLIT-AND-CLEANUP-BUG.ignore): installing the fn-valued
#     param routed through the redefinition overlap-removal, which dropped
#     the colliding caller entry, so a reuse of the name after the call
#     errored undefined_word. Required trigger: collision + a /v-parked fn
#     arg + reuse after the (non-tail) call.
def g ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) def h fn [[comp:Function v:Integer] [Integer] [v comp/v apply]] def t fn [[comp:Function] [Integer] [def a (5 comp/v h) def b (7 comp/v h) a add b]] (g/v t)
column3: caller param comp survives the first comp/v h call so the second can reuse it

column1: def myfn ([x:Integer] => [x add 1000]) def runner fn [[myfn:Function v:Integer] [Integer] [v myfn/v apply]] def doubler ([x:Integer] => [x mul 2]) runner (doubler/v) 5
column3: an fn param shadows a same-named outer fn: the body sees the PARAM, not the outer

column1: def myfn ([x:Integer] => [x add 1000]) def runner fn [[myfn:Function v:Integer] [Integer] [v myfn/v apply]] def doubler ([x:Integer] => [x mul 2]) def _ (runner (doubler/v) 5) myfn 5
column3: the outer fn is RESTORED after the frame that shadowed it tears down (no leak)

column1: def callee fn [[fp:Function v:Integer] [Integer] [v fp/v apply]] def d ([x:Integer] => [x add 1]) (callee (d/v) 5) fp
column3: the fn-valued param fp does NOT leak into the caller scope after the frame exits
